title: Desk-Break Adherence
dataSources: Posture readings (`posture:reading`), symptom logs (`symptom:log`), bathroom visits (`bathroom:visit`), sneeze events (`sneeze:event`).
app: Everyday body-signal logs — posture sensors, symptom and allergy journals, hydration-linked bathroom logs, and quirky personal counters — sent to Splunk HEC via wearables, MQTT, and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=posture:reading
| eval hour=strftime(_time,"%H"), day=strftime(_time,"%F")
| where hour>=9 AND hour<=17
| bin _time span=1h
| stats max(eval(if(state="break",1,0))) as took_break by _time day
| stats sum(took_break) as breaks, count as work_hours by day
| eval adherence=round(100*breaks/work_hours,1)
description: Measures how many working hours included a proper movement break, keeping the pomodoro promise honest.
value: Regular breaks protect eyes, back, and focus; measuring adherence turns good intentions into a tracked habit.
implementation: Ingest break events into `index=personal`; review the share of work hours with a break.
visualization: Column chart of daily desk-break adherence.
grandmaExplanation: It checks how many work hours you took a proper break in, keeping you moving through the day.
